tickets.title: Workers carry a marker and cannot dispatch through the MCP
tickets.what:
`.scratch/worker-unify/spec.md` decision 2 and the "Worker marker" and "Refusal" design. A Claude
or Codex worker sees the `hud-delegate` skill and the HUD MCP; today nothing stops it from starting another role.

acceptance.text: Every worker tab the HUD opens (pi `dispatchPi`, CLI `dispatchCli`, browser `dispatchBro` in `packages/hud-mcp/src/thin-main.ts`) is created with herdr `tab create --env HUD_JOB_DIR=<job dir>`.

With `HUD_JOB_DIR` set in the MCP's environment, `hud_create`, `hud_send`, `hud_close` and `hud_respond` return `worker_cannot_dispatch` before any herdr call, tab or quota mark; `hud_roster` and `hud_read` still answer.
`install.d/codex.sh` adds `HUD_JOB_DIR` to the HUD MCP entry's `env_vars`; rerunning the installer on an existing entry updates it; uninstall unchanged.

Tests (temp HOME/HUD_HOME/CODEX_HOME via `tmp/env.sh`): each dispatch path passes the `--env`; each refused tool refuses with the marker and works without it; the Codex installer writes the forwarded variable.
Live check by the main session after landing (not the imp): a real Claude worker and a real Codex worker each try `hud_create` and get `worker_cannot_dispatch`.

tickets.title: Any worker starts sonic with `hud-sonic`
tickets.what:
`.scratch/worker-unify/spec.md` decision 1 and the "sonic path" design: one command every
harness can run, so a worker hands a simple sub-task to sonic at the thinking it chooses.

acceptance.text: `packages/hud-mcp/bin/hud-sonic.mjs start --dir <own job dir> --task-file <file> [--thinking off|low|medium|high]` creates a sonic job through the same dispatch function `hud_create` uses (extract it; no second dispatcher) and prints the job id. `parent_job` is recorded in the child's `job.json`; its dispatching pane is the parent's `job.json` `herdr_pane` (the main session). Model and harness come from sonic's role place; `--thinking` overrides only thinking. It works with `HUD_JOB_DIR` set (ticket 01's refusal is for the MCP tools only).

`hud-sonic.mjs wait --dir <own job dir> --job <id> [--timeout <s>]` waits on the job's STATUS for at most `--timeout` seconds (default 480, `0` = check once); settled: prints the report path and report text, exit 0; failed: prints the reason, exit 1; still open: prints `still working: run wait again`, exit 3. It only waits on a job whose `parent_job` is this `--dir`. `start` never waits: several sonic jobs may run side by side.

A parent with an open sonic child is not settled, gets no quiet-job decision and is not closed (CLI judge and the pi path alike). When the parent ends its turn with a sonic report it has not collected through `wait`, it gets one fixed prompt naming the job ids to collect (pi: queued follow-up as `hud_send` does; CLI: the fixed report-prompt path).
`start` refuses when the parent job's role is sonic, and when `--dir` is not a job directory under `HUD_HOME`.

Every HUD instruction file a worker role uses (`packages/hud-mcp/instructions/*.md` except sonic's own) tells the worker it may hand a simple, fully specified sub-task to sonic with this command, picks the thinking by the sub-task, starts it early and keeps working, collects the report with `wait` when it needs it and checks sonic's result before building on it; and that it starts no other role. The generated brief (`thin-main.ts`, near the `hud-ask` path) names the absolute `hud-sonic.mjs` path.
The panel nests a job with `parent_job` under its parent's card (one indent), like native subagents.

Tests (temp homes): start/wait happy path with a fake sonic place; two children side by side; thinking override; failed child; `--timeout 0` and timeout exit 3; open child keeps the parent unsettled; uncollected report gets one prompt; sonic-parent refusal; foreign job refusal; nested card render frame test.
`hud_read` from a marked worker (`HUD_JOB_DIR` set) never marks a report read or closes a worker (see Comments).
Live check by the main session after landing: an agy imp job and a pi imp job each start one sonic sub-task and use its report.

tickets.title: HUD-run pi jobs use the HUD role text; one question rule
tickets.what:
`.scratch/worker-unify/spec.md` decisions 3 and 4. Today a pi imp reads Fishpref
`pi-roles/roles/implementer.md` (helpers `call_sonic`/`call_reviewer`, helper-pane skill), while a CLI imp reads
`packages/hud-mcp/instructions/implementer.md`. Oracle report §2 A4 and §3 B3 "Pi primary" describe the gap.

acceptance.text: pi-roles (Fishpref, `~/Fishpref/pi-roles`; commit only these files there) gains a HUD mode passed by `dispatchPi`: the role body comes from the given HUD instruction file and replaces the pi-roles body (frontmatter tools, read-only guard, model defaults stay); `call_sonic`, `call_reviewer`, `rate_helper` and the helper-pane skill are not offered. Standalone pi-roles use without the HUD mode is unchanged.
`dispatchPi` passes the HUD mode with the role's instruction file; a role without one keeps today's behaviour.

All HUD instruction files and `hud-ask`'s printed default line say: after the wait, proceed on the default only when it is reversible and inside the brief; otherwise leave that part and name it as blocked in the report.

From 02 (deferred there, 2026-11-17): in HUD mode a pi parent with an open sonic child (`parent_job` jobs not yet closed/failed; see `packages/hud-mcp/bin/sonic-jobs.mjs`) is not settled, not auto-reaped and keeps its session; when it ends a turn with sonic reports it has not collected, it gets one queued follow-up naming the job ids (the CLI side is `hud-cli.mjs`'s one fixed prompt; same wording).

From the 02 live check (2026-11-17, job j7326129a3e1b12d8): a sonic child's settlement and unread report are its parent's to collect, so `hud watch`, MCP `changes` and the bar do not tell the main session about them (no `report` token, no `[✓●]`); its questions and its failure still reach the main session; the panel keeps showing the nested card. `hud_read` by the main session still works on a child.
Tests: pi-roles HUD mode argv and tool list (no helper tools, HUD body present); standalone mode unchanged; `dispatchPi` passes the mode; instruction files carry the question rule.
Live check by the main session: a pi imp job's tool list has no `call_*`, and it can still run `hud-sonic`.
